mainTopic: The seven-substance stain test (שבעה סמנין): the משנה's rules, the גמרא's identification of the substances, and follow-up cases with soap and repeated washing
overview: The משנה finishes its list of seven cleaning substances used to test a stain on a garment. If the stain survives all seven, it is dye and the pure items handled on the garment stay pure. If it disappears or even fades, it is blood (כתם), so those items are impure and the garment must be immersed again. The משנה defines tasteless saliva, bean liquid and urine. It then requires each substance to be rubbed three times, in order and one at a time. The גמרא identifies the substances: Alexandrian נתר, בורית as a kind of אהלא (after testing and rejecting sulfur because of the laws of שביעית), קמוניא, and אשלג, which is found in pearls. Two ברייתות then add cases. If soap removes a stain after only six substances, the items are impure out of doubt. If repeating all seven removes it, items handled before the second washing stay pure, but רבי זירא rules that items handled after it are impure.

steps.title: The last two of the seven cleaning substances
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of the seven substances used to test a stain, naming the last two: קמוניא and אשלג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cimolian earth and potash.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list it started earlier: the seven substances that are rubbed on a stain to test it. These are the last two items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list itself was not the main point. It is setting up the test that comes next. Each item is a strong cleaning agent, so a real blood stain should not survive all seven.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven substances used to test whether a stain is blood

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of seven substances begun earlier in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seven testing substances end with קמוניא and אשלג.

steps.title: If the stain survives all seven, it is dye
steps.stepSummary: Someone immersed the stained garment and handled pure items on it. If the stain then survives all seven substances, it is dye, and everything stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose he immersed the garment and then handled pure items on it. Later he rubbed the seven substances on the stain and it did not go away. Then it is a dye. The pure items stay pure, and he does not need to immerse the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the first result of the test: if the stain does not come off, it was never blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood cannot survive seven strong cleaners, so a stain that stays must be dye. That means the garment was never impure. The pure items handled on it stay pure, and no new immersion is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed it in a מקוה
Ritually pure items, such as food kept in purity

phrases.english: If he immersed it and handled pure items on it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the garment with the stain on it.

phrases.english: then applied the seven substances to it
and it did not go away —
and he does not need to immerse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the seven substances just listed to give the first outcome of the test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain that survives all seven substances is dye. The טהרות stay pure and no immersion is needed.

steps.title: If the stain disappears or fades, it is blood
steps.stepSummary: If the stain disappears or even fades, it is a blood stain. The pure items become impure, and the garment must be immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the stain went away, or faded, then it is a blood stain. The pure items are impure, and he must immerse the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite result: if the cleaners affect the stain, it is blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even fading counts as a sign of blood, not just full removal. Because the stain was blood all along, the pure items handled on the garment become impure. The garment needs immersion again.

keyTerms.meaning: That it faded or grew lighter
A blood stain that makes a woman and items impure

steps.confusionAlert: You do not need the stain to vanish completely. Even if it only fades, the משנה treats it as blood.

phrases.english: If it went away, or if it faded —
and the pure items are impure,

phrases.notes: He means immerse the garment again, since the first immersion took place while the blood was still on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite outcome of the same test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain that disappears or fades is a כתם. The טהרות are impure and the garment must be immersed.
steps.whatToRemember: The test works both ways. If the stain stays, it is dye and everything is pure. If it goes away or fades, it is blood and the items are impure.

steps.title: What counts as tasteless saliva?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for a definition of רוק תפל, one of the seven substances.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is tasteless saliva?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to defining some of the substances on its list, starting with tasteless saliva. This question sets up the definitions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not just any saliva works as a cleaner. The משנה needs to say exactly which kind qualifies.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the test results to defining the substances themselves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which saliva counts as רוק תפל for the stain test.

steps.title: Defining saliva, bean liquid, and urine
steps.stepSummary: Tasteless saliva comes from someone who has eaten nothing. Bean liquid comes from chewing naturally split beans. Urine must be fermented.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the saliva of anyone who has not tasted anything. Bean liquid means chewing split beans that split by themselves. Urine means urine that has fermented.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question and adds two more definitions, explaining exactly which form of three substances qualifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each definition picks the strongest form of the substance. Saliva is from an empty mouth, beans are split naturally, and urine is fermented. With the strongest form, a stain that survives is clearly not blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Has not tasted anything, an empty mouth
Split by itself, not by a person

phrases.english: Anyone who has not tasted anything.
phrases.notes: He means the saliva of such a person, for example first thing in the morning before eating.

phrases.english: is the chewing of split broad beans

phrases.notes: Literally "divided of itself": the beans split naturally, not by someone's hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רוק תפל and defines מי גריסין and מי רגלים too.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רוק תפל is the saliva of one who has eaten nothing. מי גריסין is chewed naturally split beans. מי רגלים must be fermented.

steps.title: How to apply the substances correctly
steps.stepSummary: Each substance must be rubbed three times, in the listed order, one at a time. Out of order, or all seven together, does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He must rub each one of them three times. If he applied them out of order, or applied all seven substances together, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the rules for doing the test properly. If they are broken, the test is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test only proves something if it is done the set way: three rubs each, one substance at a time, in order. Doing it differently does not count as a valid test. You cannot learn from it whether the stain is blood or dye.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing, the act is invalid

steps.whatToRemember: The seven-substance test only counts if each substance is rubbed three times, in order, separately. Otherwise it is as if no test was done.

phrases.english: And he must rub three times

phrases.notes: "Each one" means each of the seven substances.

phrases.english: if he applied them not in their order,
or if he applied the seven substances together —
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצָרִיךְ לְכַסְכֵּס שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from defining the substances to the procedure for using them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each substance must be rubbed three times, in order and separately. Otherwise the test is invalid.

steps.title: Which natron is meant
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the נתר in the משנה is Alexandrian natron, not natron from Antipatris.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: Alexandrian natron, and not natron from Antipatris.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the substances in the משנה, starting with נתר. A ברייתא tells us which type of natron counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Natron came from different places and was not equally strong. Only the Alexandrian kind counts as one of the seven test substances. Using a weaker kind would not be a real test of the stain.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the substances listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נתר of the משנה is Alexandrian natron only.

steps.title: בורית is ice plant
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the בורית in the משנה is אהלא, a plant used for cleaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: בורית: רב יהודה said: This is ice plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the משנה, בורית. רב יהודה says it is a cleaning plant called אהלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first definition offered for בורית. The rest of this section will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaning substance listed in the משנה; its identity is debated here
Ice plant, a plant whose ashes or juice were used for washing

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹרִית. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: זֶה אַהֲלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the משנה's list to the next substance.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists בורית and ice plant separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא names 'בורית and אהל' as two items, so they can't be the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: 'בורית and ice plant'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. A ברייתא lists בורית and אהל side by side, as two separate things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בורית were simply אהל, a list would not name both. So listing them separately suggests they are different substances.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's definition from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that בורית is אהלא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists בורית and אהל as two items, so they must be different.

steps.title: New suggestion: בורית is sulfur
steps.stepSummary: Because of the challenge, the גמרא suggests instead that בורית is כבריתא, sulfur.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is בורית? Sulfur.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יהודה's definition and proposes a new one: בורית is sulfur.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sulfur is clearly different from a plant, so this fits the ברייתא that lists בורית and אהל separately. But this new idea will be tested next.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by offering a different identification.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the original definition with a new one.
steps.terutzMaskana: בורית is sulfur, which is different from אהל.

steps.title: Sulfur can't be subject to שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא counts בורית among plants subject to שביעית, but only rooted, growing things have שביעית, and sulfur has no root.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted: 'They added to them: ornithogalum bulbs, wormwood, בורית, and ice plant.' But if בורית is sulfur, does it have שביעית? Didn't we learn: This is the principle: anything that has a root has שביעית, and anything that has no root has no שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the sulfur idea. A list of things subject to שביעית includes בורית, but sulfur is a mineral with no root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of שביעית apply only to things that grow from the ground with a root. If בורית appears in a שביעית list, it must be a plant. So בורית cannot be sulfur.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contradicted': a source is brought that clashes with what was just said
The seventh year (שמיטה), when produce of the land has special rules

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost here: the second list (with לבציין and לעונין) is about שביעית, not about stains. The גמרא only uses it to prove that בורית must be something that grows.

phrases.english: Didn't we learn: This is the principle:
and anything that has no root

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new definition from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בורית is sulfur.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בורית is listed as subject to שביעית, which applies only to rooted plants; sulfur has no root.

steps.title: Back to ice plant
steps.stepSummary: Because בורית must be a plant, the גמרא returns to רב יהודה's view that it is אהלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is בורית? Ice plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the sulfur idea and goes back to saying בורית is the plant אהלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שביעית source proved בורית grows from the ground. That supports רב יהודה's original definition. The first challenge comes back in the next step, and step 14 answers it.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the sulfur suggestion and returns to step 8.

steps.title: The separate listing comes back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the first challenge: the ברייתא lists בורית and אהל as two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: 'בורית and ice plant'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we are back to 'בורית is אהלא', the original problem returns. The ברייתא names them separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא physically repeats the same challenge from step 9, because the same difficulty applies again to the restored definition.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-raises the challenge of step 9 against step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The identification of בורית as אהלא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Listing בורית and אהל separately implies they are different.

steps.title: Two types of ice plant
steps.stepSummary: There are two kinds of אהלא; one of them is called בורית, so a list can name both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two types of ice plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: there are two varieties of the plant. One is called בורית and the other אהל, so the list names both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps both sources happy. בורית is a plant (fitting שביעית), yet different enough from regular אהל to be listed separately.
steps.whatToRemember: בורית is a type of אהלא (ice plant), a rooted plant, not sulfur. It is listed separately from אהל because it is a different variety.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 and closes the בורית discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: two varieties of the same plant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate listing means בורית is not אהל at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: בורית is one variety of אהלא, distinct from the other variety called אהל.

steps.title: Cimolian earth is 'pull out, stick in'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה identifies קמוניא as the clay known as 'שלוף דוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cimolian earth: רב יהודה said: 'Pull out, stick in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next substance, קמוניא. רב יהודה gives the common name it was known by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple definition, with no challenge. It tells the learner which everyday clay the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Cimolian earth, a type of cleaning clay
'Pull out, stick in': the popular name of that clay

steps.triggerLanguage: קִמוֹנְיָא. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁלוֹף דּוֹץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next substance in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קמוניא is the clay called שלוף דוץ.

steps.title: שמואל asks sailors about אשלג
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asked seafarers about אשלג; they said it is called אשלגא, found in the holes of pearls, and removed with an iron skewer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אשלג: שמואל said: I asked the seafarers, and they said: Its name is אשלגא, it is found between the holes of the pearl, and they take it out with an iron skewer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last substance, אשלג. שמואל didn't know it, so he asked sailors, and reports their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשלג was an unfamiliar sea substance. שמואל relied on people who worked at sea. They told him its name, where it is found, and how it is taken out.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaning substance listed in the משנה
Seafarers, those who go down to the sea

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא identified the משנה's substances: Alexandrian נתר, בורית as a type of אהלא, קמוניא as 'שלוף דוץ', and אשלג as a substance found in pearls.

phrases.english: and they said: Its name is ashlega,
and it is found between the holes of the pearl,
and they take it out with an iron skewer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁלָג, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שְׁאֵלְתִּינְהוּ לְנָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next substance in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשלג is אשלגא, found in pearl holes and removed with an iron skewer.

steps.title: Soap removes a stain the seven substances could not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא: the seven substances did not remove the stain, but soap did, so the pure items are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he immersed the garment and handled pure items with it. The Rabbis taught: if he applied the seven substances and the stain stayed, then applied soap and it came out, his pure items are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה about immersing the garment. It then brings a ברייתא with a new case, where soap removed the stain after the seven substances failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a stain that survives all seven substances is treated as dye, so the pure items stay pure. This ברייתא adds a twist: soap then made the stain disappear. The ברייתא rules that the pure items are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Substances (the seven cleaning agents used to test a stain)
A kind of soap or cleaning agent
His pure items (food or objects kept in purity)

phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: he immersed the stained garment and then handled pure items with it.

phrases.english: If he applied the seven substances to it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from identifying the seven substances to the משנה's case of the immersed garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seven substances fail but soap removes the stain, the pure items are impure.

steps.title: Soap removes dye too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: soap also removes dye, so its success does not prove the stain was blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But soap removes dye too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Soap can remove dye as well as blood, so why treat the stain as blood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven substances are a test because they remove blood but not dye. Soap removes both, so its removing the stain tells us nothing. The ברייתא's ruling of impurity therefore seems unjustified.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the pure items are impure after soap removed the stain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Soap removes dye as well, so its success cannot show that the stain was blood.

steps.title: The case is where only six substances were used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: he used only six substances, then soap. The missing seventh might have removed the stain, so it may be blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is: he applied six substances and the stain stayed, then applied soap and it came out. His pure items are impure, because if he had applied the seventh substance from the start, perhaps the stain would have come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by changing how we read the ברייתא. In the case it describes, only six of the seven substances were used before the soap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full test was never done. The seventh substance might have removed the stain, which would have shown it was blood. Since he used soap, which removes both blood and dye, we cannot tell, and the pure items are impure out of doubt.
steps.confusionAlert: The ruling is impure here, not because the soap proved anything, but because the full test of all seven substances was never finished.

phrases.english: he applied six substances to it
then he applied soap to it, and it disappeared,
for if he had applied the seventh from the start,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by redefining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case (אלא): only six substances were used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא spoke of all seven substances failing and then soap succeeding.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only six were used. The untried seventh might have removed the stain, so it may be blood, and the items are impure out of doubt.

steps.title: Repeating the seven substances: items stay pure
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: the seven substances failed, he repeated them and the stain disappeared, and the pure items are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: if he applied the seven substances and the stain stayed, then repeated them and it came out, his pure items are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about repeating the full test of seven substances a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first full test showed the stain was dye, so the garment was treated as clean. Even though the second washing removed the stain, the ברייתא says the pure items stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: He repeated them (did them a second time)

phrases.english: If he applied the seven substances to it
then repeated them, and it disappeared,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא about a different follow-up after the seven substances failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seven substances fail, and repeating them removes the stain, the pure items remain pure.

steps.title: רבי זירא: only items handled before the second washing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא limits the ברייתא. Items handled between the two washings are pure. Items handled after the second washing are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: this was taught only about pure items handled between the first washing and the second. Pure items handled after the second washing are impure, since he was particular about the stain and it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the second ברייתא and limits it to items handled before the second washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the second washing, the garment counted as clean because the first full test showed dye. By repeating the washing, he showed he took the stain seriously. Once it then came out, it is treated as blood from then on, so later items are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about (limits a ruling)
He was particular, he took it seriously

steps.whatToRemember: Seven substances fail, so it is dye. Soap after only six leaves a doubt, so the items are impure. Repeating all seven and removing the stain keeps earlier items pure, but items handled after the second washing are impure (רבי זירא).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the timing of the handling decides the status. The same garment can give different results for items handled before and after the second washing.

phrases.english: They taught this only about the pure items
that were handled between the first washing and the second,
but pure items that were handled
since he was particular about it and it disappeared.
phrases.notes: By washing it again, he showed he was worried it might be blood. When it came out, that showed it really was blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the ברייתא in step 20 to a specific time window.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items handled between the washings are pure. Items handled after the second washing are impure, because he was particular about the stain and it came out.
